neighbours.label: part-versus-whole statements: where one unit (a region, a tap, a single county) takes, holds or decides a share of a larger whole; peaks on 'of' / 'the' / 'from' around 'N percent of', 'most or all of', 'the majority of'
fire: Only three times since then has one district's turnout changed the overall result.
The biggest mill consumes nearly all of the water from the upper canal.
The province is home to 9.5 million or about 70 percent of the nation's inhabitants.
The first heater switched on draws most or all of the current from the circuit.
The southern plain grows the majority of the country's rice.
One port handles more than 80 percent of the island's imports.
The main reservoir supplies nearly all of the drinking water for the city.
In just four contests has a single precinct's count altered the statewide outcome.
quiet: The district's turnout was announced late in the evening.
The biggest mill stands beside the upper canal.
The province is known for its lakes and forests.
The first heater was switched on early in the morning.
The southern plain is flat and very fertile.
One port was closed for repairs after the storm.
The main reservoir was built in the nineteenth century.
She drew a sketch of the precinct on a napkin.

short: one part's share of the whole
notes: Card: 'one state's votes affected⟦ the⟧ election', 'draws most or all⟦ of⟧ the water from the pipe', 'produces the majority⟦ of⟧ its ... food', '92 percent⟦ of⟧ Ontario’s population'; output direction promotes ' overlapping', ' partition', ' same', ' across', ' adjacent'. Probes were uneven: sentences built like the card's fired 0.27-0.46 ('60 percent of the country's people' 0.46, 'nearly all of the electricity from the local grid' 0.44, 'a single county's result decided the national vote' 0.45), but 'the bulk of the region's exports', 'two thirds of the island's population' and 'the majority of its income' stayed under 0.07.
